status: Editorial scent possibilities, not an official classification. All paths continue through examples, optional feel and references.

reviews.label: Zesty / Sparkling
reviews.reason: Lemon and lime offer distinct familiar anchors within bright citrus without inventing a separate fizzy smell.

choices.label: Lemon zest
choices.reference_note: IFF Lemon Oil CP Spain FCR: a zesty peel reference with green and juicy facets.

choices.label: Lime zest
choices.reference_note: Givaudan Lime Distilled Oil Mexico illustrates fresh lime with a sweet candy nuance; a distilled oil is not identical to a squeezed wedge.

reviews.label: Juicy / Sweet
reviews.reason: Separate fresh juicy citrus from confectionery citrus; orange and mandarin alone would add relatively little guidance.

choices.label: Juicy orange
choices.reference_note: Robertet sweet orange oil illustrates zesty, sweet peel; it does not reproduce orange juice alone.

choices.label: Candied citrus
choices.reference_note: The oil illustrates the sweet orange-peel part of the candied-peel comparison. It is not a complete candied-orange accord or a sugar smell.

reviews.label: Bitter / Dry
reviews.reason: Bitter grapefruit and aromatic bergamot give different routes beyond a single pith prompt.

choices.label: Grapefruit peel
choices.reference_note: Givaudan Grapefruit Oil USA supports a fresh citrus reference with both sweet and bitter facets.

choices.label: Bergamot
choices.anchor: The citrus scent of Earl Grey
choices.reference_note: Illustrates the aromatic citrus in Earl Grey; the tea-leaf body is a separate smell.

reviews.label: Fresh Green
reviews.reason: Retain cut grass and leaves as one useful recognition direction; splitting these near-synonyms would add nominal branching.

choices.label: Cut grass / leaves
choices.reference_note: Zeon describes a strong green, leafy character. Grass and crushed leaves are recognition comparisons, not an ingredient inference.

reviews.label: Vegetal / Sap
reviews.reason: The original combined category holds distinctly edible green vegetables and bitter resinous sap.

choices.label: Green vegetables
choices.reference_note: Zeon describes deep, diffusive, vegetable-like green. This supplies the leafy vegetable facet, not a complete pea-and-pepper reconstruction.

choices.label: Green sap
choices.reference_note: Robertet describes green, woody, resinous facets with a garlic-like nuance. Broken stalks and sap are comparisons for that green-resinous side.

reviews.label: Aquatic / Marine
reviews.reason: Fresh watery fruit and sea-air associations are meaningfully different despite both often being called aquatic.

choices.label: Watery fruit
choices.reference_note: Zeon describes fresh fruity green and melon-like character. It illustrates the green melon facet, not a complete cucumber-and-melon accord.

choices.label: Sea breeze
choices.reference_note: Firmenich Calone 918970 illustrates a stylised marine and ozonic effect with floral undertones; it is not a sample of sea air.

reviews.label: Aldehydic
reviews.reason: Offer the two familiar impressions hidden in this specialist category; neither defines every chemical aldehyde.

choices.label: Soapy
choices.anchor: A clean bar of perfumed soap
choices.reference_note: Kao describes dodecanal, CAS 112-54-9, as giving a fresh soapy-floral nuance. It illustrates one aspect of perfumed soap, not the whole bar.

choices.label: Waxy
choices.reference_note: Dodecanal, CAS 112-54-9, has sweet waxy, fatty and citrus facets. This is a different material from C12 MNA; candle wax is a comparison.

reviews.label: Clean Musk
reviews.reason: One clean laundry impression is a useful selective continuation; an unsupported clean-skin taxonomy would add complexity.

choices.label: Clean laundry
choices.reference_note: IFF describes a clean musk. Washed fabric is a familiar association that also depends on the surrounding fragrance.

reviews.label: Herbal
reviews.reason: Lavender and kitchen herbs distinguish floral aromatic freshness from leafy savoury herbs.

choices.label: Lavender
choices.reference_note: IFF Lavender Oil Maillette illustrates floral-herbal freshness, with camphoraceous and spicy nuances.

choices.label: Kitchen herbs
choices.reference_note: Robertet Rosemary Tunisia low methyl eugenol oil illustrates aromatic, fresh, cineolic rosemary. It does not supply the separate thyme comparison.

reviews.label: Cooling
reviews.reason: Mint and camphoraceous medicinal freshness are distinct enough for a novice comparison.

choices.label: Minty
choices.reference_note: Robertet Peppermint fraction oil illustrates a fresh mentholated aroma with a sweet nuance. The cool feel word is optional.

choices.label: Camphoraceous
choices.reference_note: Robertet identifies eucalyptol, CAS 470-82-6, as a fresh aromatic isolate. The eucalyptus/vapour-rub comparison describes its aromatic facet, not a therapeutic effect.

reviews.label: Anisic
reviews.reason: Aniseed, fennel and liquorice already provide convergent recognition of a specific character; keep one continuation.

choices.label: Aniseed / liquorice
choices.reference_note: Symrise Anethol Synthetic, (E)-anethole, is an aromatic anise reference. Liquorice sweets are a familiar association, not a claim about liquorice root.

reviews.label: Tea
reviews.reason: Green/floral tea and smoked dark tea offer a useful contrast without treating tannic taste as a literal odor.

choices.label: Green / floral tea
choices.reference_note: Firmenich Tea Jasmine SFE 987004 is extracted from green tea leaves scented with jasmine. It supports this particular floral-tea comparison.

choices.label: Smoked tea
choices.reference_note: Robertet Tea Black Smoked Extract Colorless cleanRscent is a named smoked-tea material. It is an example of smoked tea, not a description of all black tea.

reviews.label: Ethereal
reviews.reason: Keep one clearly named solvent-fruity comparison rather than manufacture a chemical classification.

choices.label: Solvent / pear drops
choices.reference_note: Axxence describes ethyl acetate as fruity, sweet and ethereal. It illustrates a solvent-fruity facet; pear drops are an association, not a complete formula or a sampling instruction.
